threads.thread_goal: Align on current-state findings and prioritize main bottlenecks to tackle first.

messages.text: Team, I've uploaded the first draft of the Current-State Diagnostic to A1. This summarizes the findings from our process mapping in T1. The data points to three major areas slowing us down: 1) excessive changeover time on Line 3, 2) raw material staging delays, and 3) inconsistent batch sizing. Please review and share your feedback.

Thanks for getting this out. The changeover time on Line 3 is a known issue, but the material staging delays are more significant than I realized. How confident are we in the baseline OTIF and OEE figures in A1? We need to ensure the starting point in A6 is solid before we start measuring improvements from T6.

On the material staging, the report A1 correctly notes that it's often due to late confirmations from production on what's needed next. If we can improve the scheduling visibility, purchasing can ensure the right components are ready. This ties directly into supplier lead times.
Where can I find the data for the batch sizes? I'm not sure I see it in the doc.

Good point, @472928. The baseline data in A1 was pulled from the MES and cross-referenced with finance's reports from last quarter. I've already started populating A6 with this validated data for T6. I'm confident in these numbers as our starting point.
@181683, it's in Appendix B of A1, 'SKU Run Analysis'. It shows the variance between planned and actual batch sizes.
Perfect. In that case, let's formally lock in the baseline KPIs. As for the bottlenecks, the three you've listed seem right. Let's prioritize them for Phase 1.

Great. To summarize, we are agreed on the top 3 production bottlenecks to address: 1) Line 3 changeover, 2) material staging, and 3) batch size variance. And we've confirmed the baseline KPIs and data sources for A6. I'll mark T1 as complete and move on to designing the optimized schedule in T2.

threads.thread_goal: Lock the new production schedule design and related SOP changes.

messages.text: Following up on our bottleneck analysis, I've created a draft of the new production schedule in A2. This model uses a fixed-cycle approach to minimize changeovers on Line 3. I've also outlined the corresponding SOP changes needed for T3. The goal is to standardize the new workflow. Feedback is welcome.
This looks promising. How does the schedule in A2 handle unexpected demand surges? We can't risk missing customer delivery dates. Also, what's the expected impact on overtime costs?
Will the new SOPs be reviewed by the safety team? We need to make sure we don't create new risks.

The model in A2 includes a 15% capacity buffer for demand fluctuations. I ran simulations against last quarter's sales data, and it holds up with a projected 10% reduction in overtime. The details are on the 'Stress Test' tab.

Absolutely. As part of T3, all draft SOPs in A3 will go through a formal review with the Health and Safety Officer. We'll use the validation checklist from T12, which will become our standard A7 artifact for any future process change.
The fixed cycle in A2 will definitely help us smooth out raw material calls. It makes our planning much more predictable. I'm in favor of this approach.
Excellent, the stress test results are convincing. I'm ready to approve this schedule template.

Okay, let's make it official. We are approving the target weekly production schedule template from T2 (D3). I will also proceed with drafting the full SOPs based on the outlined scope, which covers changeover, material handling, and batch control (D4).

threads.thread_goal: Agree on supplier segmentation and negotiation priorities.

messages.text: Hi all, I've completed the first pass of the supplier assessment as per T4 and uploaded the draft to A4. I've segmented them into 'Strategic', 'Preferred', and 'Backup' based on cost, performance, and risk. I've also highlighted a few 'Strategic' suppliers I recommend we approach first for renegotiation under T5. Let me know your thoughts.

Thanks @405215. The matrix in A4 is clear. I do have a question about Supplier C, listed as 'Strategic'. Their on-time delivery has been inconsistent lately, which has caused issues for us on the line. Should their risk score be higher?

This is a good framework. My main concern is ensuring we have qualified backups for our single-source materials. Does the segmentation in A4 make that clear? Also, the risk monitoring process in T11 needs to be tightly integrated with this.
That's a fair point, @261854. I weighted their cost advantage heavily, but I can adjust the risk score to better reflect the delivery performance. I'll update the sheet.

@472928, yes, the 'Backup' category is specifically for that. For each key raw material, we have at least one qualified backup identified. The work on T11 will define the triggers for activating them. The segmentation is the first step.
Good. With the adjustment for Supplier C, I'm comfortable with this approach. Let's approve the segmentation model.

Excellent. So we have approval on the supplier segmentation categories and thresholds in A4 (D5). Based on this, I will prioritize negotiations with Supplier A, Supplier B, and Supplier D to align their terms with our new production model (D6). I'll start scheduling those meetings for next week.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize implementation roadmap, pilot scope, and risk mitigations.

messages.text: Team, I've drafted the overall Implementation Roadmap and Communication Plan, now available in A5. This document outlines the phased rollout based on our discussions and covers the work in T7. I've proposed we pilot the new model on the 'Heavy Duty' product family for a 2-week period. Please review for final sign-off.

Thanks, @472928. The roadmap in A5 looks solid. The 'Heavy Duty' family is a great choice for the pilot under T9, as it uses the key processes we're changing. However, a 2-week run might not be enough to see the full impact. Can we extend it to 3 weeks to capture a full inventory cycle? Also confirming that T8, warehouse policy alignment, must be complete before the pilot starts.

The communication plan for suppliers in A5 is clear. The suppliers for the 'Heavy Duty' line are already on our priority list from T5, so this timing works well. We can use the pilot to test the new call-off process with them.
Who is going to be tracking the issues during the pilot?
@181683, as noted in A5, we'll use the Pilot Issue Log A8 for daily tracking. I will be the owner for consolidating inputs from the line leads and ensuring we address them promptly.
Extending the pilot to 3 weeks is a sensible suggestion. Let's do it. It gives us a better dataset. I've updated A5 to reflect this change. Any other comments before we approve?
Looks good to me. Ready to proceed.
All clear from my side.

Excellent. Then we are decided. The pilot for T9 will be on the 'Heavy Duty' family for a 3-week duration (D7). The overall implementation roadmap and communication plan in A5 is approved (D8). I'll update the business case in T10 with the final plan.
